text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] routing-fallbacks spike detected for routing-policy-eval (service: inference-router). 3xx failovers/s sustained. Auto-pager triggered.

sara (oncall): i'm on it, paging ben + chen. starting triage. :rotating_light:

ben (eng-sre): saw the same. high rate of policy-eval errors in validator after last config-schema rollout (~10m ago). logs show a deprecated field being accepted but reinterpreted as a different semantic default.

ben (eng-sre): short log excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T09:17:03Z ERROR policy-validator: unknown field 'fallback_variant' present, coercing -> 'default_variant' (deprecated)
2026-03-15T09:17:03Z WARN router: policy eval mismatch: expected variant 'sft-3' got 'sft-2' -> fallback to 'cpu-small'
2026-03-15T09:17:04Z ERROR router: fallback loop detected for route /v1/generate region=eu-west1
```

sara (oncall): kai / product, any customer reports?

kai (product): CS flagged 2 customers in EU with higher latency and occasional 5xx during edge bursts. not widespread but user-facing for session apps.

natalie (cs): confirmed, two mid-market customers reported degraded response times, session churn increased. asking for ETA.

chen (infra): looks like schema migration accepted the deprecated key 'fallback_variant' but our runtime mapping defaults it to a lower-capacity variant. net result: some routes implicitly fell back to CPU hosts and then triggered autoscaler thrash -> failover loops.

ben (eng-sre): root cause hypothesis: deploy introduced permissive parsing for legacy fields. permissive parsing unintentionally allowed old configs to be interpreted as explicit fallbacks. combined with canary rollout of new policy engine, led to oscillation in routing decisions between variants and region fallback.

sara (oncall): mitigation steps (live):
1) pin affected services to explicit variant override (hotfix)
2) revert permissive parsing in validator (fast rollback of schema change)
3) temporarily increase EU dedicate pool to absorb traffic spikes
4) notify impacted customers and monitor error rate

ben (eng-sre): executing step 1 now. applying override via internal flip: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-api/configs/override \ 
  -d 'service=inference-router&route=customers-eu&override=variant:sft-3&source=oncall'
```

ben (eng-sre): override applied. will validate via router logs for next 30s.

chen (infra): rolling back parser change on config-validator to strict mode (deploying hotfix-rollback v2). i'll coordinate with deploy-bot.

incident-bot: deploy started by chen (infra) - job id deploy-77821 - status: in_progress.

ben (eng-sre): monitoring metrics: failover rate dropped ~60% in last 45s, latency tail for EU improved. still some oscillation but trending down.

natalie (cs): notified customers with a brief note, describing mitigation and ETA for full resolution (~30-45m). they acknowledged.

kai (product): can we add an explicit test in the migration plan to surface this mapping change? we need a guard in rollout playbook.

ben (eng-sre): agreed. action items:
- (ben) add unit+integration test for deprecated-field mapping in validator
- (chen) add schema-enforcement pre-check to rollout pipeline
- (sara) follow up with cs on incident ticket and severity classification
- (kai) update migration playbook to require canary monitoring threshold for policy-eval mismatch

sara (oncall): handing off to ben for post-incident writeup. i'm going to sleep after the handoff. last check: error rate back to baseline for now. will reopen if seesurge.

ben (eng-sre): taking over. will produce a postmortem and link to config diff. initial mitigation timeline:
- 09:16 alert triggered by router alarms
- 09:17 oncall paged, triage started
- 09:19 override applied to pin variant
- 09:22 validator rollback deployment started
- 09:27 failovers reduced significantly, EU latency improving

chen (infra): deploy finished, validator in strict mode. pushing mesh config to prevent implicit coercions.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. assigned to ben for RCA and PM follow-ups.

ben (eng-sre): immediate customer impact: limited to EU-region traffic for customers using legacy routing policy objects; estimated affected percentage ~2% of total Hosted API traffic during window. no data exfiltration.

ben (eng-sre): postmortem next steps: gather all configs with deprecated keys, run bulk validation tool, plan migration window and opt-in compatibility mode.

kai (product): thanks team. appreciate quick responses. we'll assign CS follow-ups and prioritize migration tests in next sprint. :thumbsup:

sara (oncall): handing off completely to ben. oncall out.

ben (eng-sre): acknowledged. creating incident doc and will tag owners for action items.
